This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
Let $f(n)$ be minimal such that every set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains at most $f(n)$ many sets of four points which are 'degenerate' in the sense that some pair are the same distance apart. Estimate $f(n)$ - in particular, is it true that $f(n)\leq n^{3+o(1)}$?
#1087: [ErPu71][Er75f,p.104]
geometry | 
distances
A question of Erdős and Purdy [ErPu71], who proved\[n^3\log n \ll f(n) \ll n^{7/2}.\]

 From the way the problem is written about in the cited sources, I believe the question should say 'Let $f(n)$ be maximal such that there exists a set of $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ which contains $f(n)$ many sets of four points which are 'degenerate' in the sense that some pair are the same distance apart'.
Personally I don't find the phrase 'in the sense that some pair are the same distance apart' very clear and prefer something like 'in the sense that the set of 4 points induce less than 6 distinct distances'.
 Adenwalla
